title: How to Improve CALYPSOS | Fixing your back leg & other tips

method.teacher_system: Kayleen Babel demonstrates the components of a calypso leap, breaks down common execution errors with upper-body alignment and back-leg extension, and prescribes targeted conditioning exercises to improve technique and height.
method.signature: She breaks down the calypso by separating the front leg preparation (high chassé/lame duck and fan kick) from the back leg attitude extension, showing specific conditioning exercises for each.

practices.what: The teacher starts from the very beginning with chassés, explaining high chassé and lame duck variations.
The teacher corrects upper body posture during chassés, showing how leaning back stalls momentum.
The teacher introduces the front leg piece of the puzzle, breaking down the fan kick component.
The teacher shifts focus to the back leg problem, explaining knee alignment and attitude position.
The teacher demonstrates a wall exercise from a coupé to train back leg turnout, glute engagement, and alignment.
The teacher recommends doing sets of ten coupé-to-attitude pulses with a hold on the tenth count.
The teacher introduces a variation jumping with two bent legs to build height and energy for those struggling.

adaptations.difficulty: If floor splits are difficult and you cannot get the back leg high in the air
adaptations.adjustment: Work on flexibility and stretching on the floor first before attempting it in the air.

adaptations.difficulty: Maintaining balance and muscle engagement during back leg lifts
adaptations.adjustment: Use a wall for support while practicing coupé to attitude pulses.

adaptations.difficulty: Struggling to get height and power in the leap
adaptations.adjustment: Practice the jump with two bent legs (barrel leap/double stag) to help get hips and energy in the air.

beliefs.belief: Previous ballet training and understanding attitude position make learning calypso leaps much easier.

moments.says: The teacher welcomes everyone to the channel and introduces the topic of calypso leaps.
The teacher explains the preliminary chassés and notes common preparation mistakes before executing the leap.
The teacher demonstrates what a correct split looks like on the floor and highlights proper back leg alignment.
The teacher suggests practicing the jump with two bent legs as an alternative for those struggling with height.
The teacher reminds learners that calypso leaps share principles with other leaps and directs them to related tutorial videos.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable of improving their calypso leaps through breaking down technique and targeted practice exercises.

struggles.theme: Cannot figure out how to get up in the air
Can do all parts separately but cannot put it together

clicked.theme: Video helped improve calypsos and fix mistakes seen on camera
